metadata.title: A hypervelocity star from the Large Magellanic Cloud

evidence.quote: We study the acceleration of the star HE 0437–5439 to hypervelocity
We study the acceleration of the star HE 0437–5439 to hypervelocity

the so-called hypervelocity stars (HVS), which travel
with velocities exceeding the escape speed of the Galaxy
(Brown et al. 2005, 2006).

For HE 0437–5439, however, an ejection from the Galac-
tic centre appears problematic as the time required to travel
from the centre to its observed location exceeds the maxi-
mum lifetime of the star.

Given the fact that HE 0437–5439 is much closer to
the LMC galaxy than to the Milky Way, Edelmann et al.
(2005) suggest that HE 0437–5439 might have been ejected
from the LMC.

values.condition: Heliocentric distance adopted from Edelmann et al. (2005).

notes: HE 0437-5439: the keyword spelling (T:p1-b6) and the running-text spelling HE 0437–5439 (T:p1-b5) are typographic variants; Fig. 1 abbreviates the same target as HE0437 (I:p3-b0), so these are grouped as one star. The paper studies an already known hypervelocity star and follows up its possible LMC origin, so the contribution is follow_up. The named NGC objects and R 136 are star clusters, not additional stars; no other individual star is identified.

HE 0437-5439: T:p1-b11 reports a total proper-motion magnitude of about 0.55 mas yr−1, and T:p2-b1 reports a required total proper motion of 1.9 mas yr−1; because no right-ascension/declination proper-motion components are reported, no proper_motion_ra or proper_motion_dec values are given. T:p2-b1's 461 km s−1 is explicitly relative to the LMC, not a heliocentric/barycentric radial velocity, so it is omitted. T:p2-b1's 18 kpc is the adopted distance from the LMC centre, not a heliocentric distance, so it is omitted from distance.
